text:
As stated in previous reviews, the hardware of the camera, when it functions is fairly good. Visuals are decent enough as is audio quality. The features of being able to play music or speak through the camera are pretty cool as well.

Unfortunately, none of this makes a lick of difference due to the incredible unreliability and instability of the app that you need to download in order to operate it. 99% of the time, the visuals will freeze after a few seconds, if they come up at all, such that you have to close the app and reopen (which takes a long time) so that you can have what amounts to a still picture of your baby.

Apparently, from the reviews I read on itunes app store, this all happened after an update around Dec 2015 that introduced this newfound instability into the app. I don't know if they can simply revert to the old version of it; but from the looks of things, they're choosing to ignore the complaints and suggestions and just move on, essentially just giving the big middle finger to their own customers.

Wish I could return this, but we're stuck with having to buy a new one. Suffice it to say, I won't be purchasing from dlink ever again and will happily dissuade anyone considering purchasing from them from doing the same.

title: Not worth it.
text:
I purchased this item because I liked the idea-- a nightlight, white noise machine, clock, thermometer and nursing app all in one? And it looked cute without being too kitschy? Sign me up!

After 6 months of use, however, I am not thrilled with it. Here are the major problems:

1) The light is VERY bright-- I have to keep it covered at night, which completely defeats the purpose of having a clock.

2) The white noise is TERRIBLE. I have three white noise machines at home-- two more expensive Lectrofans (love 'em!) and one cheap SleepEasy. Both have very different sounds, but good quality. The Serenity Star, on the other hand, has a high-pitched static-y sound (which is exactly what you DON'T want for babies). I still had to go get another real white noise machine, which is ridiculous considering the price I paid for this. This was my biggest disappointment.

3) The darn thing is ridiculously top heavy! I can not tell you the number of times I have accidentally knocked it over while recording a feeding. A loud CRASH is not exactly conducive to a calm night feeding, which was the reason I was using this instead of bothering with a paper and pencil.

4) You can't display both the time of your last feeding and the temperature. You might know the approximate range (thanks to the color of the light), but if you want to know the temperature you have to figure out the correct button (which is on the back of the unit).

5) The functionality is not great. After a month or so of use it became second nature to record the feeding time or turn on the noise, but if I want to see the temperature, or change the kind of noise, or set the time, I have to turn it around and squint at the labels (or worse, dig out the manual).

Overall, the only thing that works here is the appearance (it is really pretty). Would not buy it again.

text:
My 21 month old son LOVES taking baths, but HATES getting his hair washed (due to the water that inevitably gets in his eyes). I bought this rinser with the hope that all of bath time would be fun for him (and that he didn't start draining the water as soon as I said the words wash and hair in the same sentance).

Overall, I'd say the concept is better than the execution on this product. This is probably mostly due to the wiggly toddler that I'm attempting to use it on. I try to get him to tip his head back a bit to avoid the water flow in his face. Sometimes this is successful and sometimes not. When he holds still and will cooperate in tipping his head back, this product works like a charm!! (Maybe those with older children will find more success than we did.)

We have reduced the number of tears from hair rinsing with this product. Even when he does get some water in his face, he tends to laugh about it more often than cry. He also enjoys playing with it and getting his own head wet (something that wouldn't have happened previously).

The picture quality during the day and night is pretty good. You also have the option to use the cloud service or an SD card to save the video and even without that, you can still save a picture or short video to your phone if you’re watching live and see a cute moment or whatever that you want to capture. It came with a mounting sticker and it’s on the wall pretty good. It does not rotate, therefore I only have it showing the crib since I’m mainly concerned with when he’s asleep. I really like this camera better than other expensive baby monitors. Would definitely buy again or recommend to anyone who’s looking for something simple yet effective.

title: Mid Century Modern Design - Simple & Clean
text:
I wanted to surprise my wife with a Mid Century Modern (MCM) high chair to match our home decor for my 2nd kid who just starting sitting up for his meals. We were previously using a Graco high chair that was a hand-me-down which my 1st kid used. After going through 2 kids (my friend's and our 1st), the hardware started rusting. There is a spring latch that holds the table top to the chair which has rusted. Graco should have used stainless steel screws. Anyhow, I wanted a new high chair with a table top that would be easy to wash and no worries of rusting. This high chair fitted the bill for both the modern design and easy cleaning.

Before purchasing, I read the reviews and was a little hesitant about purchasing. There were complaints about mis-alignment of screws for the step. That said, I took the plunge and purchased it. If it didn't work out, there was always the option of returning it.

Upon receiving the package, I hid it until the middle of the night when my wife had gone to bed before I started assembling. So here comes the not so nice part. Instructions were lacking and the sticker labeling the legs were all messed up. Nevertheless, as an avid DIY home fixer who never reads IKEA instructional booklet anyway, this was a piece of cake.

Steps:
1) Screw the top and bottom of the legs together. Try to match the labeled top and bottom of the legs. If the stickers are messed up like mine, I didn't think it made a difference which top went with which bottom.

2) Fix the back 2 legs to the chair. It should be labeled 3 & 4. Tighten the screws. I didn't realize the chair and numbers next to the holes till I was done. But thankfully, I fixed it right.

3) Now, for the front 2 legs. The holes for the step needs to face out. So, make sure you are screwing the legs in the correct direction. Do not tighten the screws to the chair yet. Leave the screws loosely tightened to the chair. This is very important.

4) Here comes the tricky part. Screw the step onto whichever hole you want. There are three holes on each leg. Again, leave it loosely screwed. Now, force the other side of the front leg apart until the screw holes matches up. Put in the screw and tighten it. Once tighten, go back to the first screw of the step and also tighten it. You will notice the front legs are slightly forced apart. I think it is fine and when I tested it, the chair was still stable.

5) Now, once the step is placed, go back and tighten the screw for the front 2 legs. Don't forget to tighten these screws. If you don't, the chair will be wobble.

All in all, it took me about 15mins or less to assemble this chair. I hope my personal experience above will help you with the set up and not drill additional holes.

Last, I do agree with some others who complained about the table top being hard to place in and take out. In lieu of screws and automatic table latching, I guess in order to make it tight and secure, the manufacturer had to use this method which was more cumbersome. Maybe in future they can come up with an easy yet safe design. But for now, I'm satisfied that my kid won't fall off the chair.

I was looking for a sustainable wipe to keep from using cotton or microplastics. This is a little pricey, but good. I got unscented, so I can't speak to the scent. They do just what all baby wipes do--gently wipe. I am seeing lots of silly reviews on here about it not being flushable. I hate to break it to you--you shouldn't be flushing baby wipes, anyway, unless you want to ruin your septic or your plumbing. EVEN IF A PRODUCT SAYS IT'S FLUSHABLE, YOU SHOULDN'T BE FLUSHING IT. Google it and gaze your eyes on the massive fat and buttwipe bergs clogging city sewers.

These are eco friendly because they are derived from bamboo. Not because you can flush them. It's a sustainability issue--bamboo grows fast and is easily replaceable.

title: and then my milk regulated better, and it wasn't as necessary
text: I really only used this product for the first 2.5 months of my son's life, and then my milk regulated better, and it wasn't as necessary. However, in that time, I loved it. There were times I was leaking over 2 ounces on one side while he fed on the other, and I would end up soaked no matter what I tried. Putting pressure, etc., never seemed to help. This not only allowed me to use the milk I saved, but it was also just nice not to go through pads and get my clothes inevitably soaked. I usually combined this milk with other milk that I pumped just to try to balance foremilk/hindmilk better, but sometimes I just used this in bottles, and I never noticed any issue. In summary: I loved this product and would recommend to anyone who notices a lot of leaking while nursing.

title: The magnetic key is a chocking hazzard!

My complaints are that after you open the door, the latch/hook sticks out so the person can easily get scratched if they are in a hurry and get too close to the latch. You have to be very careful with the magnetic keys. The shape and weight to the key makes it so that one can accidentally drop it multiple times. Because of this, the lid of the key that secures the magnet breaks apart, splitting the pieces into three and scattering all over the floor or under the refrigerator, which is how I lost a part of one of they keys. I had to be quick to gather them before my toddler grabbed them, as they are a chocking hazard. I tried super gluing them shut but that didn't work either. The lid and container that holds the magnet easily came off and after constant falling, the magnet itself started to chip on the edges. Not to mention, you only get two keys that you can easily lose if you're not careful. I tried to make it work but these have a terrible design flaw and are a choking hazard to babies and toddlers.

title: Baby loves. Read this before buying M or L
text:
I LOVE this swaddle. I put this on my baby while we were still in the hospital and she was asleep before I got it zipped up! She was able to wear the small until 12 lbs.

If you are looking at these swaddles and your baby is already 12+ pounds, be aware that the medium and large might be too big once you get it (even when the Velcro is as tight as it can go the baby can still get the arms out). HOWEVER, if you put a light piece of fabric/blanket behind the baby’s back and fold it over the baby’s arms and tuck it beneath their back, then Velcro the swaddle that should keep the baby snug until they fit better. There are pictures if you search for swaddle tips on the Happiest Baby blog. If you do this you will get a lot of use out of this swaddle!

The medium and large swaddles have arm holes to help transition to sleeping with arms out. Right now I have been leaving the armholes unbuttoned and if baby girl wiggles an arm out during the night it comes out the armhole.

I will put the baby in the swaddle during the day if she is a little fussy/tired and won’t settle down. She’s immediately happy (if she’s fed and dry, etc) and will smile at me while I read her a book then drift off to sleep.

Also, the baby looks so cute in these. :o)

title: Strong Velcro, good sized cup holders
text:
Purchased to add to my single Baby Jogger Summit X3 stroller for our Disneyland trip. Velcro is strong. Loaded it down with a 32oz hydro flask, a 24oz contigo water bottle in the cup holders and 2 more plastic water bottles (12oz/ea) in the middle section and the Velcro never wavered. One cup holder is larger than the other. The largest one accommodated my 32oz hydroflask. The other fit a 24 contigo which is the average size for most sport bottles and travel mugs out there. Velcro patches are large and make it easily adjust to the height you’d prefer, while still holding on with enough Velcro not to dump the organizer when it’s loaded. I gate checked my stroller on our flights and left the organizer on it. It stayed on fine. Between the cup holders is another section with a flap that Velcros closed. We tucked the flap behind to leave that slot open for more water bottles. The organizer feels like a soft sided cooler, so that middle portion would probably work to keeps stuff cool with a little cold pack.

Fabric appears to be durable, and cleans up well with a wet cloth. Zipper on the zip off pouch is a plastic, large toothed zipper making it fast and easy to unzip and and most importantly, reattach. Good call Land of the Wee. I was worried it would be an annoyance and something I wouldn’t bother with, but the large zipper makes it a breeze. The zip off pouch also has a wrist strap that snaps into place on the back. We utilized mesh pocket on the back of the organizer to hold baby wipes and hand sanitizer. That pocket wasn’t super convenient to access on my stroller because it backed all the way up to the seat back, but for the occasional need of a baby wipe or sanitizer, that pocket was perfect—much better than digging around in the bottom basket of the stroller. Since You can put the organizer on with either the pocket or zip off pouch on the front, you can decide which is more convenient to access for you.

The only color available right now appears to be the grey with white leaf/fern pattern and orange trim. My stroller is green, so doesn’t match well. I didn’t care, and actually preferred something to make my stroller stand out at Disney. When looking at a sea of parked strollers, having a non-matching (not black like all the others) organizer bag made it easy to spot.
I’m sure black is the popular color for organizers out there because it’s neutral and hides dirt. Maybe Land of the Wee will come out with black to accommodate those who are OCD about matching stuff? After 4 kids, I care less about matching and more about function.
Since ours is fairly new it’s not really dirty yet, so I can’t speak to how long it will take to get gross looking, or the durability of the fabric after being washed multiple times, but let’s be honest- how many times have you ACTUALLY washed your stroller organizers? It does wipe clean with a damp cloth pretty nicely. We had a few times when a dole whip or icream bar chocolate left a spot and we wiped it right up.

Since I don’t have kids in diapers anymore, we used the extra wet/dry bag for snacks in the park. I have stroller hooks on the handle, so we hung this bag off the handle with baggies of snacks inside. The zipper is about 3-4” from the top loop on the bag on the front. When filled and unzipped the bag sits open when hanging. Easier for my kids to see what was inside without too much fussing. The zipper on that bag is a regular sized zipper, but zips nice and smooth with a larger zipper pull than what you’d find on clothing. We didn’t load this bag with too much weight since we hung it off the stroller handle. Don’t know how much weight the bag can take before stressing the loop on the top.

Overall, I’d recommend it. It held up well and did it’s job. Nothing really stood out as an annoyance, and there wasn’t anything that I wished it had.

title: Exactly what I was looking for! Great for unusual setups - easily customizable!
text:
I needed this as a way to keep my two dogs from wandering into the kitchen or jumping on me as I came in through the front door of my apartment. As you can see from the attached picture, I have a somewhat strange setup for where I needed this gate. A pressure-mounted one would not work. I spent days (literally) searching through the different options on Amazon looking for a gate that would allow me (1) to screw-mount the gate, (2) to have mounts that did not have to be directly across from each other, (3) to have removable panels so as not to take up unnecessary space.

This is one of only 2 or 3 gates on Amazon that allows you to remove and rearrange the panels. I went with this one because it was affordable, the mounting system allowed me to not have to drill into the baseboard, and the mechanism for opening/closing is better.

This took me about 45 minutes to set up, but that was mostly due to tinkering with taking panels off and rearranging them. It wasn't difficult, just a bit time consuming. If you have an easier setup I imagine you could install this in 15 minutes or so. I do wish it came with extra wall mounts for even more setup possibilities, but overall this is an excellent product. It is sturdy and I am confident my 40lb dog won't be knocking this thing down anytime soon.

I have to say I am quite impressed with how customizable this gate is. As you can see in the picture, I was able to leave out a section of the gate so I could access the step lever for my trashcan with my foot without having to go around. I would 100% recommend this purchase to anyone who needs a longer gate with great customization options.

title: Not worth the trouble
text:
At a glance, this was perfect… But after using it, it turned out-its very troublesome. If you’re like me, I like to keep things simple and clean. I am mostly organized and wash thing by hand every day.

Why it isn’t so great:
- Moving Cover/cap is a great idea but the thickness of the straw makes it incredibly difficult to move it .. so its rarely closed. The straw it the mouth end is thicker and is a valve that’s sealed with a cut. Sorta like the blowing end of a pool tube… the kind you have to squeeze to add or lose air. So when the cover does open, the valve spring out and sprays the liquid. Imagine if you have any problems. The liquid constantly pools in the mouth end, until you flick it out.

- Which bring to my next point of cleaning. It is a nightmare. The tube scrubber they include is bent and incredibly hard to clean with, not to measure trying to rinse it with the closed valve. To rinse you have squeeze the cut valve part… multiple multiple times until you feel comfortable all the soap is rinsed.

- To close the top, it clicks into place. One day, when you have milk in there-in a hurry… you will find out why they implemented the clicking closing feature.

In the end, it became a water only container that we never use. There are perfectly cheaper, more simple and cleans faster/easier options out there. Good idea in concept but not practical in everyday life. Maybe to a zoo trip when that cover is really important.

title: HORRIBLE!
text: I absolutely hate this pump!  I went through 3 of these because I wasn't able to get my money back and could only exchange.  The motor broke twice and one time it suctioned in and never released.  Instead of exchanging it for a fourth time, I just threw the whole thing out.  The part that attaches to the motor/handle and the piece that allows milk through are impossible to clean.  Eventually, on all 3 that I went through, the milk builds up in the piece that attaches to the bottle (only takes a few pumps to fill this up) and you have to break suction for it to filter through.  It continues to do this for as long as you're pumping.  If you don't realize that the milk hasn't gone through, the built up milk gets into the motor/handle and leaks out through the suction power control.  The massage bubbles on the cup are uncomfortable and only irritate your breasts.  The suction dies down almost immediately making pumping take so much longer.  This pump is such a waste of money.  Buyer beware!

title: Decent for the money....
text:
I bought this in 2008 with my first son and used it once a week. I didn't have any complaints about it aside from the extremely loud motor. I had to use it on max setting and since one side was a little weaker, I would switch partway through. Took me about a half-hour to get out the amount I wanted. I was pretty happy with it.

Three years later, I am having some supply issues with my second son and have started using it a few times a day. I've never tried any other electric pumps and have no idea how they compare, but this thing is making me sore and I am having to pump for quite a while. I hate to buy another pump now, but I'm starting to think I need to if I want to pump daily....

Edit: Ok, after 3 days of using this 3-4 times a day, I realized it was cutting me! Definitely not made for daily use. I've switched back to my Avent manual pump for smaller, more frequent pumping sessions and am getting much better results.

My conclusion: a decent pump for the SAHM who only uses it occasionally (once or twice a week), but not for the working mom or the mom with supply issues! Spend the extra money and get a good pump.

text: The crib was easy to assemble, and it looks very nice, but BEWARE  - the paint is thin and chips very easily!! My son is 9 months, and up until recently he has slept in a pack n' play in our bedroom. We just started using this crib last week. The first morning my son woke up in the crib, I found him biting on the side rail. Not uncommon. What was alarming was the gray paint chips ALL OVER his mouth and face! The crib has a very thin coating of gray color over an oak colored wood and it flakes off very easily. I read that the crib meets all safety standards, and I pray that it means the paint is non-toxic. But because I am unsure,  I will no longer allow my baby to sleep in the crib. I wish we hadn't waited so long to use it, because I would be returning it! Looking to find some type of cover for the side rails in the meantime to try and salvage the crib. Don't waste your money here, or risk your baby's safety. Spend a little more money on a better product!

title: Good stroller, not perfect.
text:
Purchased this to use when my daughter and her family came to visit. My grandchildren were 6 months old, and 4 years old. This stroller worked well for our needs and the week they were here.

The 4 year old is quite tall, and she was able to use the standing platform and the rear seat with no problems. The stroller was easy to push and maneuver with both girls or only one. We did try it with the car seat on one occasion, but the little one really doesn't care for her car seat, so we didn't try it again. The car seat didn't seem particularly stable, though we didn't feel that it was going to fall off. We did have the 4 year old sit in the front seat, after removing the tray (which was very easy). Because she is so tall, it wasn't comfortable for her legs, and the cover was a little short for her.

The basket underneath is very roomy, though it is a pain to empty it when we needed to fold the stroller. The stroller is lightweight, easy to get in and out of the back of the van.

Our only complaint is that the front seat really doesn't recline much. I regret not getting the stroller where the seat reclined fully. However, I chose this one because of the cover, it seemed that it would provide more shade. It really did not provide much, and we tended to clip on muslin blankets to ensure there was enough shade.

I think this would be a great option for families with kids a little closer in age, or perhaps not as tall.

title: BEST TEETHER OUT THERE.
text:
After looking for (and trying) various baby teethers, I came across the Baby Banana and decided to buy one for my then 4 month old. He was at the stage where he wanted to constantly chew on something with his gums. If your baby is at the "grab and put everything in mouth" stage, THIS is the toy/teether for you. My baby is now 6 months old and this is still his favorite toy/teether to play with. It keeps him busy for a good 20-30 minutes (which all parents know is pretty crazy).

The conventional round shaped teethers are useless in my opinion. The baby can never properly fit the round teethers in their mouth and just get frustrated. This is even MUCH BETTER than Sophie the Giraffe. My baby chewed on Sophie's leg the first 2 days, and then lost interest. Theres something about the Baby Banana that he loves. It really helps massage & soothe his gums. If your baby likes chewing on your fingers or his own - THIS IS the teether to get. Its shaped just like a finger, and your baby can reach the back gums and poke it around. Round teethers won't help soothe the gums deep inside.

This thing is so baby friendly its amazing. The handles give a really good grip to the baby, and the baby can chew on both ends, as well as the handles. The peel shaped handles also allow you to put those plastic links through, so you can hang the banana onto the baby's clothes or stroller or seat, and it won't fall to the ground. (Sophie doesn't have anything to attach to).

My baby really has a go at it, you can hear the silicone squeaking against those baby gums. I'm just happy I found the PERFECT teether to soothe my baby's gums. He still doesn't have teeth yet, so I'm sure he will be able to chew off the bristle shaped head when he gets a couple of teeth.

I would buy 2, keep one at home, and one in the baby bag.

Make sure you wash the bristles thoroughly though, because little threads or fuzz can get trapped between bristles, but its very easy to clean. Highly recommend this. Probably the only teether you need!

title: Tall and skinny design makes it hard to find what you need!
text:
If I could give this 3.5 starts (instead of 3) I would! At first, I LOVED this bag, and I was always saying, "If you get a bigger bag, you just bring more stuff that you don't need!" to people who asked if I thought it was too small.

One thing you notice about the design of this bag, compared to other diaper bags, is that it is tall and skinny as opposed to short and wide. Now I know why all other diaper bags are short and wide....because, while this diaper bag DOES fit everything we need, in order for it all to fit we have to stack things on top of each other. So if you want something that's not at the very top of the bag, or if you don't pack everything pinterest-perfect every time you go somewhere, then you are frantically pulling every single thing out of the bag to get that one tiny thing at the bottom. Whereas - with a short and wide bag, it's easier to see what you have.

So long story short: I like it, it is big enough, but the design of it makes it harder to find what you need unless you are perfectly organized 100% of the time (which I am not!). So we ended up buying another diaper bag.

text: I have to say that this stroller is NOT the greatest thing since sliced bread. At least not for me. Yes, it's light. Yes, it's more compact than other double strollers and yes, it opens and closes with ease. That's where it ends for me. Neither my toddler nor my infant like the seats. They are both clearly uncomfortable. My toddler doesn't like putting her feet in the basket and squirms around everytime she uses the back seat. She does, however, like the bench although the bench isn't practical for long rides/days. Consider the basket to be completely worthless. Whether she's standing or riding on the bench, it's so low, narrow and small that it's worthless. The straps where your infant sits has no covers and digs in my baby's neck. The front seat especially just makes this whole stroller feel like a disposable stroller. Kind of like the disposable sippy cups you buy. They do the job for what you bought them for but after a few uses, you just throw em out. This stroller will be specifically just to transport my two kids at the same time. And the trip will have to be short for their comfort sake. Maybe this stroller will be as great as others say, once they both get a bit older. They are 2 years and 4 months now. I will add that the steering is good but the back wheel squeaks really loud when my toddler uses the full seat. And this has been since it was assembled. Go with the chicco if you can lift a few more pounds and don't mind the extra length.

title: Just what I needed
text:
Well, boys and girls, looks like I am the first one to review. It is not an expensive item, but it is good to know what you are getting. I do like and recommend the product. Read on for the reason for a reduction of one star.

I needed a small, 10-ounce, lightweight, leak-proof, BPA-free (not asking for too much, am I?) water bottle to carry in my purse or pocket. In other words - easily portable. This bottle fits the bill (and my pocket). It has an o-ring gasket in the lid to prevent leaks. I tested it by filling with water and leaving it upside down on the counter. It passed.

It is 300 ml (no markings for ounces), so slightly less than 10 ounces. I got the green. It is very lightly tinted, and I actually prefer it that way. The green color lid is a little different than pictured, but it is fine.

I deducted a star because they did something that I absolutely abhor in packaging. They put a big sticker on the bottom of the bottle. And not one of those that peels off easily. It comes in a box (printed in Chinese only), so why the sticker? Hot soapy water did not take the glue off. So, friends, here's the trick - peanut butter. You don't have to get the fancy all-natural oil-on-top kind (unless you already have it, then try that). My boyfriend keeps a jar of Skippy peanut butter in the refrigerator to get pine tar off his Jeep. I slathered it on the bottom, and let it sit overnight (just be sure to keep it out of reach of the dog). Next morning, I wiped it with a paper towel, and all the glue came off with it. Easy-peasy!

These are so cute and so easy to put on! My children love them so much that now my three year old can't wait to brush his teeth! He used to whine and not want to, but now he thinks it is fun! title: Excellent for Hot Chocolate; OK for Baby Formula
text:
I purchased this mixer for mixing both (but not together) hot chocolate and baby formula.

For baby formula, I found that i did an adequate job of mixing the powder with the water completely (we always use warm water before adding the powder). Here are my two critical comments about using the mixer for formula:
1) A two-speed option for the mixer would be ideal. I found that when mixing 4 oz of water + 2 scoops formula, the mixer was so powerful that the formula actually spilled out over the top of the bottle
2) The attachment needs to be longer so it can easily reach the bottom of higher volume bottle.

I use the whisk end for the hot chocolate, and find that it mixes the powder completely with the hot milk or water, and creates an amazing froth on top that helps me feel a bit like a hot chocolate snob. Here are my 2 critical pieces of advise for using this with hot chocolate (or other warm drink):
1) Immerse the whisk into the liquid BEFORE turning it on. If you turn it on and then submerse it, you will create quite a mess for yourself (and possibly personal injury depending on temperature of liquid)
2) Test the liquid level in your cup with cold/room temperature water and the mixer before adding in your hot liquid. This motor is powerful and can easily drive the liquid level up and over the top of your cup because of it's cyclonic action. I would recommend, AT LEAST ONE INCH of space between the top of your cup/mug and the top of the liquid in your cup. I first used a "standard" size mug and found that when adding 3 scoops of hot chocolate powder to 6 oz of water and mixing, the mixture was about 1/16" away from spilling over the edge of the mug.

Overall, I Like this product. For its low price, it can't be beat, just be aware of the shortcoming/limitations of it before purchasing and using it.

I know some people living in colder climates don’t like the idea of the seat staying in the car as it’s cold to put baby in but for me that’s not an issue.
This seat is built like a tank; very safe and reinforced with steel which gives an anxious parent peace of mind. I also like how slim the seat is you really could fit 3 people of these across your backseat if you needed to. If you’re looking to maximize your value and minimize your stuff this all in one seat is a good option.

title: Favorite bottle
text:
These bottles are very well made (in England!) of pyrex-type glass with smooth edges everywhere. I've dropped one from about a foot into the sink with no chips or cracks, and we can reheat ice-cold milk in it under hot running water without a problem. In fact, it seems to heat up faster and hold heat longer than the plastic version of these bottles, perhaps because the glass has a much higher specific heat (i.e. heat storage capacity) than plastic. We feel better about the glass than plastic for other reasons, too - no chemicals to leech into the milk while heating, and the milk fats don't seem to stick to the sides as much as they do to plastic.

Compared to other brands of bottles, plastic or not, we really like the compact and wide shape of these bottles. It makes them much easier to clean than standard bottles, and we like the Natural system with its nice venting and wide-based nipple shape. So, AVENT Natural gets 5 stars overall, but the glass bottles are a particular favorite.

title: Love it!
text:
I bought the Beco a little over a week ago. I've pretty much used it everyday since! I love it and so does my 7.5-month-old. He's a wee one, about 14 lbs, but long. He's always loved being worn. We have an Ergo and love it too. Before I bought the Beco I researched several of the SSC's and here is how I compare the Beco to the Ergo-

The Beco is made out of a less stiff fabric than the Ergo. It has a removable hood, whereas the Ergo does not. The biggest difference is the inside flap on the Beco that allows you to put the baby in before putting the carrier on. It's a particularly great feature for back-carrying so that you don't have to lean over with a wiggly little person on you back. The Beco is also a little more narrow than the Ergo, making it a better fit for a smaller person like me (5'1"), than the Ergo which has become my husband's carrier (he's 6'2"). The Beco also comes with an infant insert that is basically another removable flap that fits inside the carrier, as opposed to having to buy an extra insert for the Ergo.

The thing I like least about the Beco (vs. the Ergo) is that I can nurse discretely, without a problem in the Ergo, but it's much more difficult in the Beco. The hood that snaps onto the front and fits over the baby's head is pretty narrow as compared to the one on the Ergo and provides no real cover for nursing. The greater issue is the inside flap- though awesome for putting babies on our back, it fits tight against your chest and is virtually impossible to move so as to allow you to nurse.

Overall, though, I really love my Beco!

title: Best diaper system ever!
text: I had been hesitant to use cloth diapers, despite wanting to be more health and ecology minded, but the fuzzibunz have been a godsend. They are so easy, I can take them to daycare (one bag for soiled, one bag of pre-loaded clean) and there is never a fuss. The diapers are easy to clean, wonderfully adjustable, and a dream to use. I used a dozen (washed daily) of them on two boys, newborn to potty trained at three, and then handed them down to friends who used them extensively and passed them along as well. I saved money and felt wonderful about my choices and good about what was next to my baby's skin. We never had problems with diaper rash, and I'm getting ready to order another set of twelve. Friends of mine were spending the price of a twelve pack every week on diapers, and I was at home reading, knitting or sleeping, listening to the washer hum. I hung them on a bamboo drying rack overnight, and in the morning they were all ready to go.

title: Ouch!
text:
I've been searching and searching for a good moisturizer for my face to help with my troubling eczema and I definitely had high hopes after reading so many glowing reviews. I was excited to receive it in the mail but unfortunately after only a few uses it's been retired to a shelf in the medicine cabinet. The cream made my eczema patches burn. Ouch! I still tried it a few more times thinking I might be able to get used to it, but no such luck. With the burning came increased redness which is aggravating since my face is already pretty red to start. I decided further use would be pointless. Thinking that my face just might be ultra-sensitive and not wanting to waste money, I tried a little bit on some dry patches on my 4-year-old's face. She instantly started complaining and crying that it hurt. I felt terrible that this product brought her to tears!

Only positives about the products are the use of natural ingredients and a pleasant smell.

title: Big Pros Outweigh Big Cons
text:
We've been using this stroller for nearly a year and a half now. My son was 3 1/2 years old when my daughter was born and we knew we needed more than a double stroller to last us the next several years. Some of the cons don't crop up until the younger child is actually sitting in the front seat.
PROS:
1. My son loves the option to sit or stand and it's great to have a place for him to "rest" from walking or sit while eating a snack
2. Has a snack tray and bottle/cup holder for baby once they are sitting up
3. Large amount of basket space
4. Cupholder/storage compartment for adults
5. Smooth ride, navigates turns well despite length
6. Fits Graco Snugride infant carrier
7. Weighs about the same as our Graco single stroller and takes up about the same amount of space in the trunk
8. Durable, no problems and it's been loaded and unloaded and had a good amount of wear and tear
CONS:
1. Snack tray (and I think footrest as well) has to be removed when stroller is opened up or collapsed
2. Separate rear brakes unlike the Graco stroller
3. Basket is accessible only from the side when both children are riding
4. Shade doesn't provide much coverage, if any, at times and gets in the way of the older child's space
5. The five point harness is hard to get to when the snack tray is attached
6. Front seat has only two positions and the second "reclined" position makes it a little difficult for the older child to use his/her seat (and the front seat has to be reclined when using the infant carrier)

As the title says, the pros ultimately outweigh the cons. Having to remove the snack tray is a pain, the shade is fairly useless and getting in and out of the basket drives me nuts most of the time--but having a stroller that I can use with both of my kids and that they are actually happy sitting in makes it all worth it. Especially when my son was 3 1/2 it was great to be able to have a place to corral him during long errands and even now, at five years old--I love having it for anything where a lot of walking is involved. I love the large basket and I learned to get around that issue by using two small bags instead of one large diaper bag and half the time I put one on a hook over the handle bar so it is readily accessible for snacks, sippy cup, etc. This stroller could use some Graco improvements, but it has been worth the money for our needs.

title: Works!
text:
14 Aug 2021
We were very concerned when our 5.5 week old did not poop for 8 days. I saw mixed information regarding how often an exclusively breastfed baby should poop. Some said once per day, some said they can go two weeks without popping. Doctors say breast milk is such a complete meal that hardly any goes to waste. After a pediatric nurse we know said that was too long and recommended either stimulating a bowl movement by checking their temp rectally, or giving them apple juice, we decided to give the windi a go. I made an emergency run to Target. We applied coconut oil both to the baby’s bum and the windi. Since we were extremely nervous, my husband held the baby’s legs to their chest and I inserted the windi. We left it for about 20 seconds but had to abort because baby was losing their s**t. They were hungry and tired and most likely uncomfortable though not in any pain from what I could tell. I fed them and, ten or so minutes later, we set the baby on the changing table for round two when my husband noticed some poop coming out. My husband held the baby’s legs to their chest and the poop kept coming. It was relief! Highly recommend.

title: Not sticky enough, not even close
text:
I have one of those plastic standing cabinets in the garage to hold stuff the kids shouldn't get into. I wanted a way to lock it without futzing with an actual padlock. I figured that attaching this to the upper part of the door (where the kids cannot reach) would work great. Well, only after I put a lot of work into it.

First, I used the included sticky pads. After letting those "cure" for over 48 hours, I tested trying to open the doors via the handles. They popped open immediately. The sticky pads completely let go. Useless.

So I removed the sticky pads, and used some liquid nails. Again, I let it cure for a few days, and test it. Nope, still no good. Even though I scratched up both surfaces to make sure there is a place for the chemicals to grip, it let go.

On to try three. In this try I drilled a hold through the center of each base. Then I used a dremel to carve out the base to that the head of a screw could sit flush. I put a bolt in, popped a nut on, and finally, it holds! Just needed a "little" bit of modification.

Now I have a secure door, but it shouldn't have been this much work.

EDIT: OK, we just had a big trip and here are some good and bad.

title: I'm converted.update
text:
I have always used disposables with my kids. I was curious about cloth but never made the leap.

My 3 year old son is potty trained- except for Bedwetting. So for months I've been buying Good Nights, but reading up on the issue (and digging into my own memories as a kid) made me realize that this Bedwetting might go on for years. And he pees a lot. And telling him he can't even drink water before bed feels wrong to me.

I was going to get Super Undies but a lot of the reviews for them said to get these instead.

So I have. They don't leak. They don't feel soaked like disposables do (nor stink) after use. My son LOVES how SOFT they are. I don't have to worry about him putting them on backwards cuz it's the same absorbency either way. Sure they are bulky and a boring color. But I'm 2 months they will become cheaper than disposables. I do laundry daily and alternate between the two. My only concern is that they might be too hot for my son during the summer because that's a lot of fabric!

I love them so much I'm converted and I'm deciding to start cloth diapering my 7 month old daughter part time as well.

These are amazing.

Update after 1 month of use: the pull up shrunk up quite a bit, but not the extra layer, which has made it difficult for my son to use without help. Perhaps they aren't meant to be dried in the dryer, but they take forever to dry. I only bought two, they have not yet earned back their value in disposables. I have wait another month for that, but because these take so long to dry, I really need at least one more. I'm gonna try super undies. I like these but they are not helping quite the way I expected. So I doc one start

title: Great product, decent price
text:
(AMAZING UPDATE: Even though this is an update, I'm putting it at the begining of the review, because this is serioiusly an amazing thing. I accidentally washed AND dried the main unit- not the part you listen to- when my kid put it in the wash around 2 years of age. I was still able to use it for another 2 years. It finally died but my "baby" is almost 4 years old now and it was kind of melted/warped around the plug for the electricity plug in... and I left it outside a lot so that I could hear her in the yard if I was cleaning so it definitely was exposed to some elements. But it held up to a lot of abuse from me so I am definitely buying another one for our new baby.My favorite thing about it ended up being the sensitivity to sound and the visual cues. It's just super convenient if you're working out, vaccuuming or doing anything else noisy cause you can just have it in front of you and you'll notice the red lights without having to pause and check the monitor to make sure your baby doesn't need you. The baby turning over might be one or two dots, but actual crying is going to be all the dots lit up and it's hard to miss a bunch of moving red lights.)

Original post:
I love this monitor. It's a bit more expensive than whatever you'd get at a Target or Walmart- they don't actually sell it there anyway, I could only find it at BabysRus at a higher price...ick-, but it's worth it. It's really sturdy and just looks like it's been well made. I haven't dropped it yet but I think it would hold up to some pretty hard knocks, which is good when you're either moving around with it a lot, clumsy or have an older baby who wants to play with it. When you have it turned up all the way it just amplifies the background noise so it sounds a lot like my cell phone on speaker when no one is talking on the other end. During the day I can't tell if it's on or not, but at night when everything is quieter and the lights are off I can hear a light buzz. I can hear my baby turn over and sigh/scratch her head better than I can when I'm sleeping next to her! It really is very clear. Has two channels but I haven't needed to change it. I guess it's just in case there's interference from a phone or something. It has two parent monitors and you can either have them plugged in or use batteries if you are needing to be somewhere that doesn't have an outlet nearby...it can be LOUD though so I'd think even when you're in the yard if you stick one by the door, you'll know if something's up. I like the built in night light with auto-off feature, but we got this soothing sea horse cuddle/night light thing that she uses instead till she's asleep... We got it for her at 13 months cause she had trouble at bedtime, let her play with it during the day so it didn't get associated with "the horrible time of day when everyone wants to leave me"(bedtime), then gave it to her at night...works like a charm! Satisfies that need to DO SOMETHING, but sneaks in a calm down thing. She turns it on at night by herself, falls back asleep and I don't have to get up most of the time. If you don't have a troubled sleeper, the night light on the monitor is just fine! title: Attractive storage for child's room
text:
This is a cute storage unit for a child's bedroom. It is made of real wood, and once put together, is an attractive piece of furniture.

The one thing I have a doubt about is the wheels. I'm not really sure why this product HAS wheels, because it isn't really a storage cart that one would wheel around a work room. The wheels also seemed loose to me; I don't know if this was a problem with my assembly of the product or if that's how they were supposed to be. In any case, we're using the locker as a nightstand for my 4 year old, so it doesn't need to move around much.

Assembly went smoothly: all of the pieces are labeled clearly, and the labels match the visual instructions. Note that there are no words describing what to do, but I found that the pictures were clear enough that one didn't need words. I was able to assemble it myself, too; no need for a second pair of hands. All of the pieces lined up as they were supposed to and there were no problems with screw holes in the wrong place, etc., so compared to some other pieces of kids' furniture we've assembled, this one is a low-frustration piece.

title: The BabyKeeps pacifier holder works great for my son and bonus-- the prints are awesome ...
text:
The BabyKeeps pacifier holder works great for my son and bonus-- the prints are awesome and the colors are vibrant! I have used other brands of pacifier clips when my other boys were little but the clips weren't nearly as strong. My boys would always pull them off their clothes and we would loose pacifiers at the park, out on walks or at the store. Well, not this time! The clip on them is very tight and holds well to all sorts of fabrics (stroller straps, winter jackets, regular cotton tee's). The 3 pack is perfect for us, too. I have one for around the house and another clipped into the car seat for when we're out and about, which leaves a spare one always clean and ready for use. I have washed these clips in the washer with our kids regular laundry and they wash great... just lay flat or hang to dry so they don't curl up.

I would recommend these clips to anyone looking for a quality and cute solution to countless paci-drops! I did receive this product at a discounted rate in an exchange for my honest review. The discount that I was given didn't sway my review in any way. My review is honest and based on my own experience with the BabyKeeps pacifier clips.

title: Just get it
text:
10/10. I have owned several strollers (most recent baby jogger Citi Mini GT2 in double and single).

Pros:
— Very nimble.
— Excellent storage space.
— The only stroller I could find that has a piggyback/glider option WITH an actual space for my growing toddler to hold onto without hitting her head. It's comfortable for all of us and she loves it.
— Seat can be adjusted to have them sit "far" up. In my Citi Mini GT2 strollers you couldn't adjust the seat other than making in flat. It was frustrating and ultimately uncomfortable for my toddler because she wanted to sit-up more and see the world. Though I did love how far back it reclined — great for a nap. Fortunately, the seat in the Cruz can also recline quite well.
— Comes with two covers and a belly bar.

Cons:
— Price. HOWEVER, I took a risk and ordered a "like new - open box" option on Amazon at a $150 discounted rate. When I received the package the box was pretty banged up, but the stroller was BRAND NEW. I did the same thing for the glider and saved $20. Very happy about this!
— My toddler fits fairly well in our Baby Jogger GT2 but is a little "snug" in the Cruz. It's a bit less roomy IMO, but she still seems to be comfortable. I was considering the Vista but chose the Cruz given her age and preference for walking. I feel confident in my decision.
— Not necessarily a con, but I prefer the fold (how simple it is) in the Baby Jogger GT2 better (absolutely not a deal breaker).

I would purchase this again.

______
I would have given this a 5+++ star but sadly the pail has broken on me twice. the first time the inside metal sliding piece got stuck half way open -- which really defeats the purpose of having two closures to keep out the smell. luckily that fixed itself somehow after a few weeks. however, just a week ago another piece broke -- this time it was the hinge on the opening. it broke completely (see photo) and now I will have to get a new diaper pail after only 5 months.

if i didn't have these issues, i would have given this a great review. i love the paid overall in terms of effectiveness (really don't smell the diapers, can hold a lot of diapers, you can use any garbage bag so you don't have to pay for expensive refills) and looks (modern design is really nice and love the grey color).

i'm hoping that Bubula will do the right thing and send me a replacement to stand behind their product and prove that this is an unusual situation to have multiple pieces break after just 5 months.

title: Can't be installed safely without purchasing extra overpriced accessories, if at all
text:
Three instructions state that the bracket screws must penetrate 1" into solid wood or a stud. But studs are 1.5" thick, while the brackets are 2". So you'll need an extra several sets of drywall anchors even if you can hit a stud on one side, which they sell at a ridiculous $4/2 anchors. And if you have base boards, pony up another $12 for spacers, unless your baseboards are large in which case you need two sets.

I thought I'd be ok since I've got solid door frames at the top of my stairs. But the gate has some give in it, so they require 6" from it to the top of the steps. So I'm back to square one and the overpriced spacers and anchors.

They also sell a banister post kit. Better hope your banisters are at least 6" back from your stairs (yeah right!), unless you want a hole between the gate and the stairs!

title: How the heck do you get it back in the bag?
text:
So far LOVE this pack 'n play/ bassinet/ changer. The one I have is actually pink and black but it's the same exact thing. My baby hasn't come quite yet, but I have family (within driving distance), and we don't have a room for her just yet (her crib wont fit in with us) so I wanted something that was travel friendly and compact enough to fit in the room. I also Love the wheels so you can move it from room to room. Folds out and back up easily once you get the hang of it. The little holder that clips to the side is really flimsy as another reviewer stated but everything else is really sturdy. I even put a bit of my weight on there and nothing gave way or made any noise in indication that it might give way.

The mat is really solid. I've read a few other reviews of different brands that said the mat didn't have much support and their baby could feel the bars through the mat.

All in all so far it's pretty great. But I still have about a month to go before she gets here so I went ahead and (TRIED) to pack it back into the bag it came with. On the instructions I guess they put in to include their higher end models which apparently have a different carrying bag because it says there's an accessory pouch and then the main bag. The bag that came with this one is just a flimsy little rectangular bag. I can't seem to fit anything more than the mat and the play yard into the bag without it busting at the seams. Which I don't have a problem using an extra bag to carry everything else but it kind of defeats the purpose of the "easy travel system" that these things were designed for if I need to carry it in separate bags. I mean, what if the extra bag gets lost?
Also, there's two little pieces that connect the changer to the play yard and they certainly LOOK like they can be disconnected from the changer. They even have little tabs you can pull back to "release" them, but mine won't come out which makes it even harder to fit most everything into the bag as these stick out about 3-4".

I managed to get everything back in but the diaper holder, which I can do without, after staring at it like a puzzle for 20 minutes and doing a little crafty thinking. I was wondering if anyone has managed to successfully put everything back into the bag without the bag looking like it was about to rip?

title: Love these bottles.
text:
I love, love, love these bottles. I use the kids versions myself because they're smaller and easier to carry, and of course, I'm clumsy and these are leak proof. I also like that because they have the leak proof valve, they're a bit slower to drink from and my backwash doesn't end up in the water, unlike the bigger adult Contigos. I could drink too fast from those and start coughing. The adult sized ones also spray water when the spout opens, and if they've been in a cold car and brought inside, they'd shoot a bunch of water out when opened, whereas the kids ones doesn't seem to have that problem. These are quite durable, they've taken hard drops from my buttery hands, and the only reason I'm replacing my old one is because I've lost it!

These are filled with water 24/7 and so I do not clean them for days at a time as I only put purified water in these. When it is time to clean them, I clean the lid and spout with a cotton swab and isopropyl alcohol to kill germs, and then I'll splash some alcohol in the bottle, give it a couple rinses, and then back to drinking out of it. I do this with all my Contigos and I've never had any problem with mold.

The spouts on the Contigo are so comfortable and easy to drink out of, that it's the only water bottle I'll ever use. I've had many other water bottles, most of them are cheap plastic ones I got for free from events, others are nice aluminium ones I was gifted, but I would use them for a day, and then put them away and never use them again. My earlier Contigos have got some mileage on them and have been across the country a few times, and they're still perfectly fine.

I kinda wish the handles on these had the carabiner clip thing like the adult ones have, but that's not a big deal. I do wish I could get permanent marker to not rub off on the lid from when I tried putting my name on them. Also, can we get fun graphics on the 20oz versions like the 14oz ones have? Please?

title: I want to love it, but "meh"
text:
I have mixed feelings about the Tripp Trapp. I don't know if there's another similar high chair out there that I would like better, but I wish I had looked more extensively at the Keekaroo just in case.

Pros: small footprint, useable for the long haul, not just a year or two, fits nicely at our small dining room table (in our small house), easy to clean up, sturdy, the chair is relatively easy to adjust

Cons: THE HARNESS - it is still huge on our 9 mo old (30% for height/weight) and I find it very difficult to adjust. When we first started putting her in the chair around 5 months, just to sit with us, even with the harness on the smallest possible setting, the plastic plate at the back of the straps would hit her in the back of the head/neck, so we didn't use them - we just made sure we were right next to each other always. I know it's only recommended for 6mo+, but even now at 9 mo, when she can stand up in the seat, we rarely put the straps on (and just stay next to her) unless we have to get up to get something because they are such a pain to get on, off and adjust. In fact, it's too tight for her currently, but I can't adjust it with her in it to tell how much larger to make it, so I have to guess when she's not in it.

We didn't bother buying the cushions (though we do have the infant plastic insert) - another reason I wonder if the Keekaroo would have been better. It's a hard seat, but she doesn't seem to mind.

It's not ideal not to have a tray if you have a round dining table like we do, especially since baby has always had finger food and regularly feeds herself; if we had a rectangular table it wouldn't be such a mess. He was able to take naps on his own for a few weeks, but currently (8 weeks), he won't sleep longer than 20-30 minutes on his own. It is so nice not being glued to the couch or bed.

Lastly, this carrier has given us so much freedom. My son won't just sleep in a stroller or stay asleep in a car seat. We couldn't go to any social function or restaurant without screaming and crying. Now, as soon as we get to any restaurant, we put him in the boppy and he sleeps like a dream. This carrier allows us to live our lives!!!! 10/10 would purchase!!

title: Same as daytime diapers - don’t waste your $!
text: I have used the Bambo brand since my daughter was born in 2016. They were beyond fantastic. One diaper for both day and night. Then our son was born April 2020 and we continued to use the same brand. But then within the last year or so Bambo decided to jump on the let’s revamp our product and up the price but offer less quality train. Both their day diapers and night diapers are exactly the same. They’re both thin and their absorbency is minimal at best. We were so fed up with them we decided the best way to be eco friendly is to potty train our son which we since have at least than 2 years old (we did not use the ridiculous 3 day method which btw is a crock of crap, your baby WILL NOT be potty trained in 3 days. Instead we bought potty training underwear and used those, when he peed he could feel it similar to a cloth diaper and he got the concept within a few weeks). Our son who will be two next month still uses diapers for his one nap (lasts 2-3 hours) and his overnight sleeping (7:30pm-7am). In these Bambos he wakes up soaked every single day, bed sheets wet, pajamas soaked. It’s ridiculous what they are charging for a less effective product which honestly feels intentional. I reached out to them on Instagram, not much to say. I mean what can they say when they’re selling a product that is far inferior to their previous product. They’re diapers! Just leave them alone and if you absolutely must be greedy then charge more for the product that already works! We are expecting our third child in just a few days, we will be using cloth diapers because at least we know what to expect there and using elimination communication to get our baby potty trained as soon as possible. Our daughter (now six) was potty trained by 1, using sign language so it’s possible. I never leave reviews but after cleaning up our sons bed for the 5th time this week I had enough and ordered proper overnight pull-ups.

title: Great way to keep your toddler safe while shopping
text:
My children are grown now, but when this came across my idea list, I had to write about it.

So many people snarkily say this is like putting a dog leash on your children. So? You use a leash on your dog to keep them safe. Why is it so offensive to use a similar item to keep your child safe?

Anyone who has actually had a toddler knows they move like liquid mercury. One second, they are hugging your leg, the next second, they are trying to flush their shoes down the potty. You cannot hold their hand 100% of the time, especially when you are out shopping.

Shopping is when this product shines.
The facts are, there are a lot of evil people out there who have the goal of kidnapping children. Don't make it easy for them! Make sure you'll know if someone tries to touch your child!

I had twins. Now, imagine if you will, twin toddlers, each wanting to go a different direction at all times. Poor mama just wants to put something in the cart or heaven forbid, check out a new top at the mall. Malls are nightmares for losing a toddler. They can duck under a rack of clothes and disappear in seconds! These harnesses (and they are harnesses, not leashes) keep your child no farther than the end of your own arm. That is a GREAT thing!

Grocery stores... oye. Trying to manuever a cart and actually put food in it is a challenge with twin toddlers. These created safe trips for me. I don't know about you, but I see tiny ones, who's heads are bigger and heavier than their little bodies (in other words, every toddler on the face of the earth), trying to stand up in the front seat area of those carts. MANY a toddler has fallen OUT of those carts, smacking directly on to those hard grocery store floors!!
I didn't want mine to be one of those with a concussion or worse; I used these types of harnesses to hook them into the cart so they couldn't stand up. It made for safer shopping trips with a lot less worry!

You might not have twins like I did, but I'm sure you want your sweet pea to stay safe and near you at all times. These products help you do that. An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure... in other words, prevent a disaster or accident if you can, and these bring a lot of peace of mind.

title: Levana continues its state-of-the-art baby monitoring
text:
Things have certainly changed since I last had a little baby, 6+ years ago. The two monitors we used back then were audio only, and were somewhat adequate when it came to determining whether the baby needed checking on.

This Levana Ovia camera/remote is an amazing improvement, albeit an expensive one!

On the camera side: finding an adequate place to either mount it or position it on a table, within reach of an a/c outlet, keeping the power cord out of baby's reach, is the initial challenge. Note, though, that this isn't JUST a camera. It's capable of playing lullabies, and of transmitting your voice from the remote. The lens also rotates side-to-side, and up-and-down, and does so very quietly. There is also a fair-to-middling zoom feature.

On the remote side: the hand-held remote has the look of one of today's smartphones or videogames. It's deceptive in that way, because it has screen icons like you'd see on your ipad, but they are not touch-sensitive. They're controlled by the little directional dial down on the lower right hand corner of the device. I don't know how many times I've poked at, or tried to drag the icons, only to remember to go back to the thing in the corner. After downloading the manual and quickly reviewing it, I was able to navigate around the features very easily. Once the remote was fully charged, I disconnected it from the power cord and carried it around, and discovered the limits of the signal range fairly quickly: so, I can't take the remote out on the front porch on a nice day!

This Ovia unit has a lot of features that are really nice, but certainly not essential to "baby monitoring". You can tell the camera to snap still photos, or take video, you can talk to your baby through the camera, you can have it play lullabies.... there are elements of this contraption that make me think of security/surveillance, which I'm not too comfortable with. Although more and more our world is filling up with surveillance cameras, I'm not sure I want one of the first things the baby gets familiar with is a wall-mounted surveillance camera! The lullabies/voice feature just call attention to something I'd rather the baby not be aware of. But that's just me.

I'm impressed with the quality of the camera image, even in low light, and its ability to pick up sound. Although where I've mounted the camera I can see the entire crib, it's nice to be able to point the camera elsewhere if needed.

Also of note: no manual. it would have been nice if there was something in the packaging saying: manual available at >>>.
The website was a little strange to navigate (no results returned when I searched on "Ovia", for instance), and the manual finally turned up in a place I wouldn't have expected.... but once I found and downloaded it, it made sense.

[most of this review is identical to my review of the Levana Keera model. Other than a different camera design, and a black remote instead of white/silver, I can't find much of any differences between the two. One night, when using this Ovia, though, the remote showed a real lack of battery staying power. It would be nice if the battery could last, say, for 8 hours, instead of the ~3 that I got out of it the other night. It doesn't feel as much like a remote when you have to plug it in to the wall.

Additionally, it would be nice if the cameras had a battery feature, maybe where they could have two AA batteries, for the occasions when you just don't have a safe and convenient option for plugging them in.]

4.5 stars.

For now, though, if you are comfortable with the price, and the product specs (especially the signal range) look good to you, this is a great buy.

title: Accurate Fit
text: Fits a 24 mm flange very well and securely. Have to make sure it’s pushed in snugly, but definitely a good solution if your pump’s manufacturer does not carry flanges in your size.

title: Not what it was cracked up to be
text: This is a cute little car seat. Other than that…..it’s heavy. Significantly heavier than a traditional car seat. We started using this car seat 2 months ago and already the base is not locking/unlocking correctly. I have attempted to call customer service but nobody answers and you have to leave a message. So as of right now, I have a car seat but no base. Also the button to loosen/tighten the chest straps isn’t flush anymore with the carseat(which doesn’t seem like that big of a deal, but it’s loose and that can’t be good) currently I have a very expensive car seat that doesn’t work and I don’t feel like my baby is safe in it. As you can see in the photos, it doesn’t matter if the car seat is in the base or not it stays locked/unlocked.

title: Poor Quality
text:
With a travel system this cheap, you get what you pay for. On sale it was $160 I believe. So take that into consideration when buying. However, I feel that the majority of Evenflo's products on the market are junk. From their travel stuff, down to the toys and bouncers.

The material in both the stroller and the car seat is rough and there is absolutely no cushion. I can tell it is uncomfortable. The stroller is nearly IMPOSSIBLE to open without two people. To open it, you literally grab the handles, hold it outward, and thrust it open by shaking it. I can't tell you how many times I've had people in public hilariously stare at me while I'm shaking this thing around like a crazy person. It opens if someone holds the bottom part still while you shake the handles. But its ANNOYING! You shouldn't need two people.

Also, there is no shade for the front of the stroller. The canopy does not swing forward. It stays in one position at the top. So if you're walking outside and the sun is shining it's about impossible to keep your child shaded. And don't push this thing through grass, rocks, or dirt because it's junk. Even on the pavement it sounds like the wheels are going to fall off. Cheap plastic.

The button to release the carseat from the base constantly gets stuck. You really have to push it in and shake it/pull up to get it out. The one good thing about the base is it's pretty easy to get into vehicles that have the metal hook pieces slightly exposed in seats. It's very easy to install into Chevy Equinox/Traverse, however, the Ford vehicles are a pain in the a** because the metal hook pieces that the clips go on to are sunken way down in the seat and it's very hard to latch to them.
